flows.summary: Map a repo as user flows, steps and code by listing its entry points, handing briefs to independent passes, checking their citations and voting them into one map.

steps.name: Person lists every entry point the repo exposes, found from code by the framework adapters
steps.notes: Adapter chosen per [[entry]] in flowmap.toml (or config.detect_entries); here the cli adapter turns every top-level flowmap/*.py with a __main__ guard into a command. inventory.endpoints takes a reader so lens can inventory any git revision, but this CLI uses the worktree reader.

steps.name: Person writes the brief for one independent mapping pass, filled in for this repo
steps.notes: Fills flowmap/RUN_SPEC.md with the stack text for each configured adapter and the vocabulary (or discovery-mode text). The brief itself is then handed to an agent outside the CLI, whose output is docs/flowmap/runs/<run-id>.json.

steps.name: Person checks a pass's citations and coverage against the code and the inventory
steps.notes: Read-only; the result is the printed BAD/MISS lines and the exit code.

steps.name: Person votes the independent passes into one map, plus the questions where they disagreed
steps.notes: Also reads docs/flowmap/inventory.json, the run JSONs and (optionally) docs/flowmap/decisions.json. Human decisions come back in through decisions.json and flowmap.toml vocabulary, not through this command's arguments.

flows.summary: Look at the finished map: Mermaid diagrams at three zoom levels, an interactive atlas, and a left-to-right canvas of screens, flows, code and data.

steps.name: Person generates Mermaid diagrams of the map at system, flow and step zoom
steps.notes: Needs map.json and inventory.json (reads them in Diagrams.__init__) and builds the full call graph to decide what is plumbing.

steps.name: Person builds the interactive system atlas page from the map and the call graph
steps.notes: UI is the generated page; its generator is atlas.build (template atlas.template.html). atlas.data reuses the Diagrams class and calls d.system() only to fill d.matrix. split_votes re-reads QUESTIONS.md that reconcile wrote.

steps.name: Person draws the map as one left-to-right canvas of screens, flows, steps, code and data
steps.notes: --from reads an existing atlas page instead of building the data; --out can redirect the file. UI is the generated page; its generator is canvas.main/graph.

flows.summary: Review a code change by where it lands on the flow map: place it, write and check the story, render the change page and share a link, with a hook that does the placement automatically after a push.

steps.name: Author places a diff on the flow map and reads the verdict, touched steps, reach and blind spots
steps.notes: Pure read: prints Markdown (or --json). Builds the call graph at both base and head from git, re-inventories entry points at both, and compares both against map.json.

steps.name: Author prints a change's deterministic facts as JSON to write a story from
steps.notes: change --facts: prints the facts and returns before anything is written. The story (docs/flowmap/changes/pr-<n>.story.json) is authored by the agent/person from this output, outside the CLI.

steps.name: Author checks which claims in the story the facts do not back
steps.notes: change --check: prints problems as JSON and exits 1 if any; writes nothing. Still computes the full facts first.

steps.name: Author renders the change as chapters on the map into a single HTML page
steps.notes: Reads docs/flowmap/changes/<name>.story.json if present (else auto-chapters from the graph). Lint problems are only warnings here; they block --link. UI is the generated page (template change.template.html).

steps.name: Author prints a viewer link that carries the whole change page in its fragment for the PR body
steps.notes: change --link: re-renders and writes the page, then prints the link (to stdout) or refuses when lint problems exist. It trims diff text to fit the PR-body budget. Nothing is published; the viewer is static.

steps.name: Author paints a change's reach onto the atlas
steps.notes: atlas --pr <base>..<head>=<label>. Same entry point as build-atlas; overlay is the extra work.

steps.name: Author paints a change and its story chapters onto the canvas
steps.notes: canvas --change <name>=<base>..<head>; also reads docs/flowmap/changes/<name>.story.json to number chapters on the cards.

steps.name: After a push or PR creation, the hook places the branch's PR on the map and has Claude post the summary comment
steps.notes: Not an inventory entry point (bin/ is not the cli adapter's commands dir). It shells out to `flowmap lens`, and `post` creates or edits the PR's single flow-lens comment on GitHub (external state, not a Model).

flows.summary: Build the static, data-free change viewer so teams can host their own and render change links in a browser.

steps.name: Operator builds the hosted change viewer page with no data in it
steps.notes: Imports flowmap/change.py (and so lens, graphs, atlas) just to get the template with its CSP; the produced page makes no requests.

flows.summary: Ask the static call graph which entry points reach a piece of code, dump the graph, or check that every handler is walkable.

steps.name: Developer counts or dumps the call graph, in the working tree or at a git revision
steps.notes: callgraph with no argument prints counts; `callgraph dump [<ref>]` prints JSON (via lens.graph_at for a ref).

steps.name: Developer asks which entry points and flows can reach a symbol
steps.notes: callgraph impact <file:sym>. Needs docs/flowmap/map.json, so it only works after reconcile.

steps.name: Developer checks that every entry point's handler is a node the call graph can walk from
steps.notes: callgraph check: exits 1 when a handler's file is parsed but has no such node ('broken').

observations: `CLI flowmap callgraph` (flowmap/callgraph.py:__main__) and `CLI flowmap change` (flowmap/change.py:main) are each one entry point that fronts several unrelated intents chosen by argv/flags (dump / check / impact / summary; --facts / --check / --link / render). The inventory cannot tell these apart, so I had to repeat the same endpoint in several steps.

`--link` still renders and writes the change HTML (flowmap/change.py:main) although its documented job is only to print a link; `--facts` and `--check` return before writing. Same command, three different write behaviours.

reconcile writes QUESTIONS.md as prose and atlas re-parses it with a regex to recover split votes (flowmap/reconcile.py:write_questions_md writes it; flowmap/atlas.py:split_votes parses it). State round-trips through Markdown.

flowmap/atlas.py:data calls Diagrams.system() only for its side effect of filling d.matrix (comment: `fills d.matrix`), so the atlas depends on the Mermaid diagram generator's internal state; flowmap/diagrams.py:Diagrams.system reads as a pure render but mutates the object.

flowmap/reconcile.py:main is one long function that votes flows, clusters steps, scores evidence, clusters endpoint-less steps, builds map.json and drives two renderers; by far the busiest single hop.

Several modules evaluate config at import time (flowmap/lens.py MAP/CODE regex, flowmap/diagrams.py ENGINE_ROOT/PLUMBING/APP_DIRS, flowmap/atlas.py OUT, flowmap/verify.py ROOT), and flowmap/viewer.py imports flowmap/change.py:viewer_html, which drags in lens, atlas, graphs and config just to read a template. Running the viewer builder needs a valid repo config.

flowmap/change.py:facts, flowmap/lens.py:analyse and flowmap/canvas.py:main all recompute overlapping facts (changed symbols, graph at base and head, endpoint sets); change.facts even calls lens.analyse for the verdict after recomputing most of it itself. lru_cache on lens.graph_at is what keeps this affordable.

Three overlapping notions of 'app code': config.graph_files/graph_roots ([code].graph), config.app_dirs (adapter roots plus other) feeding lens.CODE, and the adapter-specific file listings in flowmap/adapters/cli.py:_files. A file can be in one and not the others (bin/ is `other` only, so bin/flowmap-pr-hook is not an entry point and is not in the call graph).

Symbol-definition detection exists in multiple places with different rules: flowmap/verify.py:anchor_ok (regex), flowmap/lens.py:defs (builder.symbols or ts_symbols/rb_symbols regex outlines) and flowmap/graphs/python.py:symbols (AST). A citation verify accepts may not be a node the graph knows.

flowmap/diagrams.py still hard-codes an app-specific `workflow engine` notion (ENGINE_ROOT from [flows].engine, text mentioning `executor.run_workflow`) in an otherwise generic tool; this repo sets no engine, so that branch is dead here.

flowmap/callgraph.py:endpoint_flows reads docs/flowmap/map.json, so `callgraph impact` crashes before the first reconcile, while `callgraph check` and the plain/dump forms do not need it. The dependency on reconcile's output is invisible from the command list.
